text:
Microsoft's Recall feature became a privacy scandal in 2024 because it was initially designed to screenshot the user’s screen every few seconds and store that data locally, effectively acting as a "photographic memory" for the PC [Source: ev-1]. The controversy escalated when security researchers demonstrated that these screenshots were stored unencrypted (in plaintext) within a local SQLite database, contradicting Microsoft’s claims of encryption [Source: ev-1]. In response to this backlash, which marked the AI PC era's first major privacy crisis, Microsoft delayed the launch in June 2024 and fundamentally changed how Recall operates [Source: ev-1].

The revised version is now opt-in (default OFF) rather than enabled by default [Source: ev-1]. To access the timeline of screenshots, users are required to use Windows Hello authentication and presence detection [Source: ev-1]. Additionally, the updated feature excludes incognito browsing sessions and DRM-protected content from being captured [Source: ev-1]. This modified, opt-in version reached general availability on Copilot+ PCs in 2025 [Source: ev-1].
